t: You're looking at the Vaudeville Theatre, on the Strand. It first opened in 1870, mostly staging vaudeville shows and musical revues. It has been rebuilt twice, though each new building kept parts of the one before. What stands now dates from 1926 and seats 690. Inside, some early stage machinery survives, including rare thunder drums and lightning sheets. The architect was Charles J. Phipps, who designed more than forty theatres in the later nineteenth century, so he's one of the quiet makers of the West End.
